This looks like a print artefact; the 0.81 percent fact is review only and the figure-printed value stays in visual.json.

Anti-AMPAR antibodies are said to be found in serum and CSF, but the serum titer is below 1:20 and the antibody is described as only found in the first CSF sample taken in Germany. Whether serum was positive is unresolved; no resolution is inferred.

The abstract states about 200 days on the intensive care unit while the case text states 220 ICU days; the abstract value is described as approximate and the stay is recorded from the case text. This is treated as rounding, not a source conflict.
Three cycles of bortezomib are reported as administered, and the therapy was then interrupted after septic shock and CMV-associated pneumonia; whether all three cycles were completed is not stated.
The sentence on the follow-up mGLUR5 titer of 1:1 does not state whether the sample was CSF or serum.

The authors state the clinical improvement cannot be ascribed to daratumumab alone because of sequential immunosuppression including bortezomib, and that spontaneous healing must be considered; improvement and daratumumab are ordered but no cause is asserted.

The sentence giving the admission-day intubation does not say which admission; it follows the transfer to a secondary care center but this is not stated, so no order between transfer and intubation is recorded.

The flow cytometry monitoring sentence says CD38 detection is difficult after daratumumab because the drug blocks common antibodies; the absence of CD38-positive cells is therefore recorded as an observation with the authors alternative interpretations, not as proven depletion.

Relative times use both "onset" and "disease onset" (and once "symptom onset"); "onset" and "disease onset" are read as the same reference point because the article uses them interchangeably for the same course (7, 16 weeks and 12 months after onset; 28 weeks, 9 and 18 months after disease onset).
Figure 1 shows a care-location bar labelled Iraq before the secondary care center in Germany; the text never names where the first hospital admission took place, so no location fact is recorded.
